ai.description: *Draco maculatus* reaches 20 cm. It features a grey-brown body with dark spots and orange-yellow patagia marked by black blotches. Distinctive features include a pointed snout and a prominent throat fan.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Draco maculatus* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, black-spotted throat patch in males, which is absent or differently patterned in other Indian *Draco* species.
ai.habitat: *Draco maculatus* inhabits tropical evergreen and moist deciduous forests, typically residing in the canopy of trees at elevations ranging from sea level to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Spotted Flying Dragon is primarily diurnal, using its patagia—wing-like skin folds—to glide between trees to forage for ants and termites while avoiding ground predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Draco maculatus* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 2–5 eggs in a soil nest. Breeding typically occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months (April–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: *Draco maculatus* is found in Northeast India, primarily across the foothills of the Eastern Himalayas and the hills of Assam, typically at elevations up to 1,500 meters.
